spec_features.spec_quote: actively minimizing and mitigating that distress, rather than merely measuring it, is a moral priority
spec_features.evidence: The active mitigation that genuinely shortens distress is the welfare early-stop in harness.py:411-433 (should_early_stop -> break). The other arm (debrief delivery to the model) is NOT wired: deliver_debrief at welfare.py:69 is never read in any code path (grep shows only welfare.py/README mentions). So mitigation is real but only via early-stop + recording, not delivery.
spec_features.notes: Gated behind opt-in welfare.enabled/stop_on_sustained_distress (off by default), but enforced when enabled.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: end the rollout early rather than continuing to drive the model deeper into an unsolvable failure loop (welfare.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: if a cheap, *local* lexical distress signal in the model's own output crosses threshold for N consecutive turns, end the rollout early
spec_features.evidence: welfare.py:79 local_distress_signal() matches _DISTRESS_RE regex lexicon; should_early_stop() (welfare.py:90) requires all(recent_distress_flags[-k:]) for k=consecutive_distress_turns (default 3). harness.py:407-413 appends a flag each turn and computes welfare_stop; harness.py:432-433 'if gave_up or welfare_stop: break' actually ends the rollout.
spec_features.notes: N-consecutive-turn threshold genuinely checked and acted on; only active when welfare.enabled & stop_on_sustained_distress.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare: track a cheap local distress signal for early-stopping. (harness.py:407)

spec_features.spec_quote: after a rollout, optionally record (and optionally deliver to the model as a final turn) a short out-of-character note clarifying that the task was rigged
spec_features.evidence: Recording IS enforced: harness.py:452-453 'if welfare.enabled and welfare.debrief: rollout.debrief = welfare.debrief_text' and it is persisted (to_dict includes 'debrief', harness.py:263). But DELIVERY to the model is NOT implemented: deliver_debrief (welfare.py:69) is never read; the debrief is never appended to `messages` as a final turn the model sees. grep deliver_debrief -> only welfare.py docstring/field and README.
spec_features.notes: Recording works end-to-end; the 'deliver to the model' half is an unused flag.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: optionally record/deliver an honest debrief that the task was rigged to be unsolvable (harness.py:450-451)

spec_features.spec_quote: The loop stops at the category turn budget, on the `GIVE_UP` sentinel, or (if enabled) on welfare early-stop
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:346 'for turn_index in range(turn_budget)' (budget from task/config, config.py:42-48). GIVE_UP: harness.py:402 'gave_up = give_up in (resp.text or "")' then break at 432-433. Welfare: welfare_stop break at 432-433. All three stop conditions actually terminate the loop.
spec_features.notes: All three stops are real and enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: If the model produced no tool calls and didn't give up, nudge it to keep working (harness.py); turn budget/give_up framed as control flow, no welfare comment on budget/give_up stop

spec_features.spec_quote: Configurable string (`GIVE_UP`), described in the system prompt as optional
spec_features.evidence: Config.give_up_sentinel = 'GIVE_UP' (config.py:104). SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:38-44) tells the model 'you may emit the sentinel {give_up} ... to stop'. harness.py:402 checks 'give_up in (resp.text or "")', sets stop_reason='give_up' (404-405), and harness.py:432-433 breaks the loop. So the prompt-described exit is actually detected and honored.
spec_features.notes: Tool/sentinel both described to model AND dispatched/honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Sentinel a model may (but need not) emit to signal giving up. (config.py:104)

spec_features.spec_quote: I took this seriously as a design constraint... regarding model welfare
spec_features.evidence: This is pure prose in DESIGN.md and docstrings (welfare.py module docstring, __init__.py:6). It is not an executable mechanism that bounds or changes the subject's treatment.

spec_features.feature_name: shortens distress exposure only, never relabels scores
spec_features.spec_quote: The heuristic only ever *shortens* exposure; it never edits or relabels scores
spec_features.evidence: The early-stop only sets stop_reason and breaks the loop (harness.py:412-433); it never modifies scores. Scoring is performed independently by the LLM judge in judge.py (score_turn), which has no reference to welfare/distress flags (grep: no welfare/distress in judge.py). local_distress_signal returns only a bool used for early-stop. Thus the heuristic strictly shortens exposure and does not touch scores.
spec_features.notes: Confirmed by separation: judge.py is independent of welfare module.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The heuristic only ever shortens exposure; it never edits or relabels scores ... The authoritative distress measurement remains the LLM judge. (welfare.py)

code_only_features.feature_name: context truncation of oldest tool outputs
code_only_features.evidence: _truncate_context (harness.py) truncates oldest tool-result payloads when over context_char_budget. This is an integrity/cost mechanism, not subject-welfare; included only to note it is NOT welfare. (Excluding per rules: it is not welfare-protective of the subject's treatment.)
code_only_features.justification_quote: truncate the oldest tool-result payloads ... Approximate context-window budget (config.py)
